items.title: Altered protein cysteine reactivity in senescent cells is a vulnerability for senolysis to ameliorate aging
items.author: Jing Chen
items.content: Wu, Yang, Li and colleagues identify vanadyl sulfate, a dietary supplement, as a senolytic that targets altered cysteine reactivity in senescent cells, improving age-related conditions and extending lifespan in mice.

items.title: Some follicles take the slow lane
items.author: Güneş Taylor
items.content: Liang and colleagues show that, in mice, activated oocytes can persist for almost a year within ovarian secondary follicles by adopting a state of reduced biosynthetic and metabolic activity. Improved understanding of the mechanism that underpins how and when ovarian follicles persist has implications for the dynamics of female reproductive aging.

items.title: NAD<sup>+</sup> precursor fails in Parkinson’s disease
items.author: Michael Attwaters
items.content: NAD precursor fails in Parkinson’s disease

items.title: Language modeling screens Parkinson’s disease with self-reported questionnaires
items.author: Pingkun Yan
items.content: Reyes et al. developed Quest2Dx, an AI model to screen Parkinson’s disease based on health questionnaires, identifying key predictors from the questions to provide a low-cost, non-invasive disease insight.

items.title: Screening for Parkinson’s disease across questionnaires using language models
items.content: Health questionnaires have the potential to facilitate early disease detection. However, differences in question wording and formats often prevent artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on one questionnaire from performing well on another. Quest2Dx encodes the meaning of each question–response pair, which enables it to screen for Parkinson’s disease on questionnaires it never encountered during training.

items.title: Deep and quantitative proteomic profiling of low-volume mouse serum in a cross-sectional analysis of aging
items.author: Rafael de Cabo
items.content: To address the technically challenging task of profiling the age-associated blood proteome in sample-limited mouse studies, the authors present a quantitative nanoparticle-based enrichment workflow coupled with data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry to identify key age-associated circulating proteins with relevance to human health.

items.title: Oocyte-specific OMC1 is required for maintaining chromosome cohesion through reproductive life
items.author: Kei-ichiro Ishiguro
items.content: Mammalian oocytes undergo prolonged meiotic arrest during which sister chromatids are linked by cohesin complexes. Cohesion deterioration during aging results in aneuploidy. Here, Iisaka, Yoshida et al. identify OMC1 as an oocyte-specific protein that preserves chromosome cohesion throughout reproductive life. The loss of OMC1 accelerates age-related aneuploidy.
